comparison: Perfect agreement on structural claims (C3, C43-C53). Both evaluations find the cryo-EM structural observations from published literature well-supported. Peer reviewers accept these structural claims without challenge; their concerns focus on validating physiological relevance through mutational analysis, not on the structural data itself.

Disagreement on D215 mutant genetic data (C54, C56-C59). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by genetic data showing Ssu- phenotypes. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to critical experimental design concern: the ratio of mutant to wild-type protein in 40S ribosomes after glucose shift is unknown, undermining confidence in attributing phenotypes specifically to mutant protein.

Disagreement on D215L ribosome profiling data (C60-C62). OpenEval finds polysome and subunit data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers group this with other D215 in vivo data and rate UNCERTAIN due to the same concern about mutant vs. wild-type protein ratios affecting interpretation.

Disagreement on D215 mutant eIF1 and context discrimination data (C65-C73). OpenEval finds Western blot and reporter assays SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting that while data are not directly criticized, the fundamental concern about mutant protein incorporation affects interpretation of all in vivo phenotypic data.

Disagreement on D215L leaky scanning data (C74-C82). OpenEval finds el.uORF1-GCN4-lacZ reporter data SUPPORTED and methodologically sound. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the data are not directly criticized but noting the mutant protein incorporation concern affects all in vivo reporter assays.

Partial overlap on R225K and E144R data (C83-C85). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers include C83-C84 in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of leaky scanning data due to mutant protein ratio concerns, and separately question the mechanistic interpretation (C85) about indirect interface effects.

Agreement on D215L biochemical data (C86-C95). Both evaluations find the in vitro TC binding kinetics SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the data provide direct biochemical evidence for PIN destabilization. Peer reviewers accept these purified mutant 40S experiments without question, as they avoid the mixed population concern affecting in vivo experiments.

Disagreement on R219 mutant genetic and reporter data (C96-C100). OpenEval finds Sui- phenotypes SUPPORTED by reporter and growth assays. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting data are presented clearly but the concern about mutant vs. wild-type protein ratios applies to all R219 mutant phenotypes.

Disagreement on R219 context discrimination data (C101-C104). OpenEval finds Western blot and reporter data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to the same mutant protein incorporation concern affecting interpretation of R219 mutant phenotypes.

Disagreement on R219 leaky scanning and mechanistic interpretation (C105-C108). OpenEval finds el.uORF1 reporter data SUPPORTED, though notes electrostatic repulsion hypothesis (C108) is speculative. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN for in vivo data and separately question whether phenotypes result from specific interface disruption or misfolding (C108 in R10).

OpenEval finds R219 polysome profiling data (C109-C110) SUPPORTED, showing translation initiation defect rather than ribosome biogenesis defect. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

Disagreement on S223D phenotypic characterization (C111-C114). OpenEval finds reporter, Western blot, and specificity data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting data are extensive and internally consistent but the mutant vs. wild-type protein ratio concern limits confidence in attributing effects to S223D.

Disagreement on S223D dual Sui-/Gcd- phenotype (C115, C118-C120). OpenEval finds polysome, subunit, and GCN4-lacZ data SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers include these in vivo experiments in their UNCERTAIN evaluation due to mutant protein ratio concerns, and separately question mechanistic interpretation (C120 in R10).

Agreement on S223D TC binding without mRNA (C121-C124). Both evaluations find the biochemical data SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the interpretation of POUT destabilization is reasonable. Peer reviewers accept these purified mutant 40S experiments without question.

Agreement on S223D kinetic analysis (C125-C133). Both evaluations find the in vitro biochemical data SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the interpretation of accelerated POUT-to-PIN transition is well-reasoned. Peer reviewers accept these direct biochemical measurements as they avoid mixed population concerns.

Disagreement on main conclusion (C4-C9, C137). OpenEval finds the integrated conclusion SUPPORTED by combined genetic and biochemical data showing opposing phenotypes provide strong evidence for physiological relevance. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, finding the approach and data supportive but raising concerns about possible misfolding and mutant protein levels; they suggest compensatory mutations are needed to validate the interface model.

Peer reviewers provide a cross-cutting UNCERTAIN evaluation for mechanistic interpretations (C42, C85, C108, C120), questioning whether phenotypes result from specific interface disruption or from misfolding/altered domain orientation. They request compensatory mutation experiments. OpenEval addresses these claims individually within other results but does not group them as a separate mechanistic concern.
